description: We are a team of two Electronics and Communication Engineering students, passionate about Embedded Systems, IoT, AI/ML, and innovative problem-solving. For NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, we are developing ASTRA – Astronaut Smart Tracking, Risk Assessment & Assistance, a health-monitoring solution for astronauts. We welcome enthusiastic teammates with skills in Python, AI/ML, UI/UX design, web development, data visualization, or healthcare research who are eager to build something impactful!
summary:
**ASTRA – Astronaut Smart Tracking, Risk Assessment & Assistance** is an AI-assisted astronaut health monitoring and decision-support platform designed for long-duration space missions. It integrates health data from sensors, manual self-assessments, and historical records to help astronauts monitor key indicators such as heart rate, SpO₂, body temperature, sleep, physical activity, mood, and stress.

ASTRA analyzes changes against an individual's health baseline, highlights unusual trends, and presents understandable insights through an interactive dashboard. It also connects health indicators with the five hazards of human spaceflight: space radiation, isolation and confinement, distance from Earth, altered gravity fields, and hostile environments. The platform provides alerts, preventive-care suggestions, and guidance on when to seek medical support.

By combining Embedded Systems, IoT, Python-based analytics, and AI-assisted assessment, ASTRA aims to make astronaut health monitoring more accessible, informative, and proactive. It supports crew self-awareness and informed decision-making when immediate medical assistance from Earth may be limited.
details:
ASTRA is an AI-assisted astronaut health monitoring and decision-support platform designed to support crew members during long-duration space missions. It addresses the challenges of monitoring physical and psychological health in an environment affected by space radiation, isolation and confinement, distance from Earth, altered gravity fields, and hostile closed environments.

How it works: ASTRA collects health information through sensor-based inputs, manual self-assessments, and historical health records. It monitors indicators such as heart rate, blood oxygen saturation (SpO₂), body temperature, physical activity, sleep duration, mood, and stress. The system analyzes measurements against an astronaut's personal health baseline, identifies unusual variations, visualizes trends, and generates understandable health insights, alerts, and preventive-care recommendations. Its interactive dashboard enables astronauts to review their health status and determine when medical support may be needed.

Benefits and intended impact: ASTRA promotes proactive health awareness, supports early identification of unusual health trends, organizes health information, and helps astronauts make informed decisions when immediate medical assistance from Earth may be limited. Its offline-first design direction also supports operation in communication-constrained environments.

Technology and tools: The software prototype uses React.js, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, Python, FastAPI, SQLite, SQLAlchemy, NumPy, Pandas, and Scikit-learn. The proposed hardware integration uses an ESP32 microcontroller with MAX30102, MPU6050, and suitable temperature sensors. MQTT and REST APIs provide communication between the hardware and software. A simulated telemetry mode allows the application to be demonstrated without physical hardware.

Creativity and innovation: ASTRA combines embedded sensing, IoT, AI-assisted personal-baseline analysis, interactive health visualization, and spaceflight hazard awareness in one platform. Rather than displaying raw measurements alone, it aims to explain health changes and provide actionable guidance.

Engineering considerations: Our team considered sensor limitations, data reliability, personal health variations, privacy, offline operation, usability, and the need for explainable alerts. ASTRA is designed as a decision-support prototype and does not replace professional medical assessment or mission-specific medical protocols.
